mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST MoM change < -0.5% and RSAFS MoM change < -0.3%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) triggers restrictive monetary policy, increasing equity discount rates and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO is above 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105.0 indicates economic contraction, reducing corporate investment and earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO falls below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k jobs.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0 and FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.10%.
